code.description:
The problem code of its error (`SH1002`), or of its failure when
it ran and failed on the setup (`doctor`); `shuyi explain <code>`
prints its page.

error.description: Why it could not run, if it could not.

help.description: How to fix it, with the code.

limits.description: What it could not determine, in plain words.

ok.description:
Whether it passed: nothing found by a check, runs that agree, a
game made, a toolchain complete. False too when it could not run.

result.description: What it found or made; absent when it could not run.

Ci.description: What CI does with a target's exporter.

oneOf.description:
It only checks the game against the target (`check --target`): the
package is built elsewhere, and `why` says why.

beside.description:
What `shuyi.ron`'s `export.beside` copied into the package, from the
export's folder, a folder with the bytes of all its files.

debug.description:
With `--release` on Windows and Linux, the program with its debug
sections, kept beside the package and never in it
(`game-0.1.0-linux.debug`).

edition.description:
The edition of `shuyi.ron`'s `editions` it built, if any:
`exposure-report.json` says what it was built from.

folder.description:
The folder the package was made from, from the export's folder:
what `--run` runs.

out.description: The export's folder, as the game shows it.

pack.description:
The pack of the game's files the program reads, from the export's
folder with its size, if the build is packed (a release desktop or web
export of a package with a `packed` feature): beside the program, or in
a `.app`'s `Contents/Resources` (ADR-0110).

package.description:
The package, from the export's folder: a zip, a `tar.gz` or a
folder.

profile.description: The target profile its check ran with.

recipient.description: With `recipient`, the closed build's copy made for them.

sizes.description:
The package's size first (for `web`, its zip's), then each program
in it.

ExportPlan.description:
What `export --plan` answers: the packages a release of the game makes.
Each target of `shuyi.ron` no exporter builds is a limit of the answer.

exports.description:
Each exporter of each target, targets sorted by id and a target's
exporters in the order they are registered.

prerelease.description: Whether the version has a pre-release part (`1.2.0-beta.1`).

version.description:
The version the packages carry, as `export-report.json` writes it:
`shuyi.ron`'s `app.version` when it sets one, else the package's.

ExportResult.description:
What `export` answers: a package's report, with `plan` the plan, or with
`detect_recipient` the marks found. Only its schema is read: [`export`],
[`plan`] and [`detect`] each answer one.

FileSize.description: A file of the export and its size.

file.description:
The file, from the export's folder (`game-0.1.0-windows.zip`,
`game-0.1.0-windows/game.exe`).

code.description: The code it holds, if it holds one.

file.description:
The file it is in (in a package, its path there; in a pack, the
pack's and the picture's).

said.description: What was read, in a few words.

Given.description: A copy the ledger says was given.

build.description: The SHA-256 of the base package.

date.description: The day the copy was made.

label.description: Who they are, as the ledger says.

overlay.description: The SHA-256 of the copy's package.

Host.description: The runner a package builds on in CI.

Level.description: How bad a target problem is.

oneOf.description: The game doesn't fit the target: the check fails.
It fits, short of what the target recommends.

MarkKind.description: Which mark a code was read from.

PlannedExport.description: One exporter of the plan: what CI does with it, and where.

ci.description: Whether CI builds it or only checks it.

container.description:
The image it builds in, if any (the Steam Linux Runtime's for
`linux`).

profile.description: The target of `shuyi.ron`'s `targets` it checks (its profile).

why.description: Why CI only checks it, for `check-only`.

RecipientCopy.description: A recipient's copy of a closed build (`export --recipient`).

build.description:
The SHA-256 of the base package, the public one (a folder's: of
`sha256sum`'s lines for its files).

code.description: The code their copy carries: 8 characters of Crockford's base 32.

ledger.description: The ledger it was written in, from the game's folder.

marks.description: The marks it carries, each in a few words.

note.description: That a mark is circumstantial evidence, never proof.

out.description:
The copy's folder, from the game's folder:
`dist/recipients/<id>/<target>`, with its `export-report.json` and
`exposure-report.json`.

overlay.description: The SHA-256 of the copy's package.

package.description: The copy's package, from its folder.

codes.description: The codes the marks name, each once.

file.description: The file read, from the game's folder.

ledger.description: The ledger read, from the game's folder, if there is one.

marks.description:
Every mark read: each program field, each pack's layout, each
picture.

note.description: That a mark is circumstantial evidence, never proof.

recipients.description: The copies the ledger says carry those codes.

signed.description:
Whether the ledger's signature verifies against its signer; none when
it has no signature or there is no ledger.

verdict.description: What the marks say together: "no mark found", or the code they name.

oneOf.description:
Signed by no one (`codesign --sign -`): Apple silicon runs it, and
the player opens it once with Open Anyway.

TargetCheck.description: Which check found a target problem.

oneOf.description: The frame at its scale fits the display.
The smallest text is tall enough.

The required actions of each screen bind to distinct inputs of the
target.

On a one-bit display, every role has patterns and the roles that
tell things apart stay distinct.

TargetProblem.description: A problem of the game on one target.

actions.description: The actions a controls problem is about, by name.

inputs.description:
The inputs a controls problem is about, as the keymap file names
them (`East`, `East+West`).

message.description: What is wrong, with the numbers.

roles.description: The palette roles a one-bit problem is about (`team.player`).

screen.description: The screen a controls problem is about, if one.

setting.description:
The game's setting it is about: in `shuyi.ron`
(`targets."playdate".frame`), the keymap file's table for the
target (`keymap targets."playdate"`), a screen's declaration
(`screen "title"`), or the skin's pattern map
(`files/palette@onebit.ron`).
